Mozilla today announced several new features for Firefox's AI Smart Window, which is still in testing phase. Details below.

Firefox Smart Window adds new features

A few months ago, when Mozilla first unveiled Smart Window, it described the feature as "a standalone, optional window in Firefox that lets you interact with your chosen AI assistant while browsing the web," and said it could "summarize, compare tabs, organize information, or ask questions, all without leaving your workflow."

Since then, the company has been gathering user feedback and today announced a set of new features aimed at "helping people finish what they started online."

Starting today, Firefox's Smart Window will suggest groups of related tabs, so that when you're researching a topic or planning an event, you can keep up even as the number of tabs keeps growing. One particularly useful new feature is automatic duplicate tab detection, allowing users to find and close duplicate tabs with one click.

Smart Window now also benefits from a new partnership between Mozilla and Exa, also announced today. Exa is an AI-focused search and web retrieval company. After integrating with Smart Window, it can "pull in the latest web information and show the sources in the answer, without having to jump to another search results page," Mozilla said.

Finally, Smart Window also lets users enter natural language prompts, such as "that running show I watched last week," and promises to "show previews of pages from your browsing history, so you can more easily find the page you're looking for among similar results, without having to open each one to figure out which is which."
